findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "cbam_list_countries" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Returns the origin countries that have their own table in the official CBAM default-values act, as ISO code and name, with the regulation source. Use it to pick…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "trade_list_quotas" appears informational but accepts parameters (history) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: cn, country, order_number, celex, history, cursor, limit

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "tenders_list_watched" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

Each change has the listing (names, aliases, type, programmes, countries, listin" → after: "Returns additions, amendments and removals between official sanctions list snapshots: US Treasury OFAC SDN and Consolidated, UK HM Treasury/FCDO and EU Financial Sanctions Files. Use it to monitor what changed since a date; use sanctions_search_entries when you have a name, and sanctions_get_entry w"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
